valueDimensions.label: Autonomy
valueDimensions.description: Steering your own life by your own compass, and having room to make decisions that are genuinely yours.

valueDimensions.label: Connection
valueDimensions.description: Feeling close to people who know the real you, and being present for the ones who matter.

valueDimensions.label: Growth
valueDimensions.description: Stretching past who you were yesterday and getting better at things you care about.

valueDimensions.label: Security
valueDimensions.description: Having enough stability and predictability to feel your feet under you.

valueDimensions.label: Contribution
valueDimensions.description: Doing work or offering care that makes a real difference beyond yourself.

valueDimensions.label: Health
valueDimensions.description: Tending to your body and mind so you have the energy to live the rest of it.

valueDimensions.label: Creativity
valueDimensions.description: Making, building, or expressing something that carries your fingerprint on it.

valueDimensions.label: Integrity
valueDimensions.description: Acting in line with what you believe, even when it costs you something.

valueDimensions.label: Adventure
valueDimensions.description: Seeking novelty, challenge, and experiences that make you feel awake.

valueDimensions.label: Recognition
valueDimensions.description: Being seen and valued for what you bring, and having your effort acknowledged.

patternTags.label: Avoidance
patternTags.description: Sidestepping the hard thing in the moment, even when a part of you knows it will cost more later.
patternTags.supportiveNote: Almost everyone avoids something; noticing the pattern is the first move toward loosening its grip.

patternTags.label: People-Pleasing
patternTags.description: Managing other people's comfort at the expense of your own needs and honest opinions.
patternTags.supportiveNote: This usually starts as kindness turned all the way up, and it can be turned back down with practice.

patternTags.label: Perfectionism
patternTags.description: Holding a standard so high that finishing, shipping, or being seen feels unsafe.
patternTags.supportiveNote: The care underneath perfectionism is real; the goal is to keep the care and drop the tax it charges you.

patternTags.label: Self-Criticism
patternTags.description: Speaking to yourself with a harshness you would never aim at someone you love.
patternTags.supportiveNote: A loud inner critic is common and learnable to answer back; you are not stuck with the volume it came at.

patternTags.label: Rumination
patternTags.description: Replaying the same worry or regret in loops that feel like problem-solving but rarely resolve.
patternTags.supportiveNote: The mind loops when it cares; there are workable ways to give it an exit instead of another lap.

patternTags.label: Overcommitment
patternTags.description: Saying yes to more than any one person can carry, then running on fumes.
patternTags.supportiveNote: This often comes from being capable and generous, and it responds well to a few honest boundaries.

patternTags.label: Comparison
patternTags.description: Measuring your insides against other people's outsides and quietly coming up short.
patternTags.supportiveNote: Comparison is a near-universal reflex, and it loosens once you notice how rigged the measurement is.

patternTags.label: All-or-Nothing Thinking
patternTags.description: Seeing things as total success or total failure, with little room for the middle where most of life happens.
patternTags.supportiveNote: This is a common mental shortcut, and the gray area gets easier to see with a little practice.

patternTags.label: Fear of Failure
patternTags.description: Letting the possibility of getting it wrong shrink what you are willing to attempt.
patternTags.supportiveNote: Fear of failing usually means you care about the outcome, and courage is a muscle that grows with reps.

patternTags.label: Need for Control
patternTags.description: Feeling safe only when you are holding all the variables, and tense when you cannot.
patternTags.supportiveNote: Wanting control is a reasonable response to past uncertainty, and it can soften as trust gets rebuilt.

questions.prompt: When you picture a version of the next year that actually feels good, what is at the center of it?
questions.helpText: Go with your gut, not the answer that sounds most impressive.

options.label: I am learning fast and becoming someone I respect more.
I feel close to my people and genuinely present with them.
My life feels stable and I am not bracing for the next shock.
I am making or building something that carries my mark on it.
I am doing something new and a little bold that makes me feel alive.

questions.prompt: You are facing a genuinely hard decision. What do you find yourself reaching for first?

options.label: The option that keeps me free to change course later.
The safest option, the one least likely to blow up on me.
The option that lets me look at myself honestly afterward.
The option that keeps everyone around me happy and settled.
I stall. I gather more information until the moment almost passes.

Replaying conversations and decisions long after they are over.
